record.paper_title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Prescribing a compact zero-measure aperiodic set
record.original_question: Fix 2n ≥ 6. Let H_0 on R^{2n} \cong C^n be the quadratic Hamiltonian H_0 = ∑ λ_j |z_j|^2 defining an irrational ellipsoid, where the coefficients λ_j are positive and rationally independent, and let K \subset (0,∞) be a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero. Does there exist a C^∞ Hamiltonian H: R^{2n} → R that is C^0-close to H_0 and isotopic to H_0 through a compactly supported isotopy, such that for every energy value a \in K the level {H = a} has no closed trajectories of the Hamiltonian flow? Equivalently, can one realize an arbitrary compact zero-measure set K as a set of aperiodic regular energy values for such a perturbation of H_0?

evidence.quote: An irrational ellipsoid M in the standard symplectic vector space Cn is the unit energy level of the quadratic Hamiltonian H0 = P λj |zj |2, where the eigenvalues λj are positive and rationally independent.

It appears plausible that the function H0 can be modified as in the proof of Theorem 3.1 simultaneously for all energy values from a compact zero measure set K ⊂ (0,∞). The resulting function H will then be smoothly isotopic to H0 and have K as the set of aperiodic values. This leads to the following Conjecture 3.4. For 2n ≥ 6, there exists a C∞-function H : R2n → R, C0-close and isotopic (with a compact support) to H0, such that the Hamiltonian flow of H has no closed trajectories for energy values in the set K.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 3$ and identify $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ with $\mathbb{C}^n$ via the standard symplectic structure. Fix positive real numbers $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ that are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, and consider the quadratic Hamiltonian
$$H_0(z_1,\dots,z_n) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^n \lambda_j |z_j|^2,$$
whose level sets are irrational ellipsoids. Let $K \subset (0,\infty)$ be an arbitrary compact subset of Lebesgue measure zero. Decide whether there exists a $C^\infty$ function $H:\mathbb{R}^{2n}\to\mathbb{R}$ with the following properties:
(i) $H$ is $C^0$-close to $H_0$;
(ii) $H$ is smoothly isotopic to $H_0$ through an isotopy with compact support (i.e., the isotopy equals $H_0$ outside a compact set);
(iii) for every $a \in K$, the level set $\{H=a\}$ is a regular level on which the Hamiltonian flow of $H$ has no closed trajectories.
Equivalently, can every compact zero-measure subset of $(0,\infty)$ be realized as a set of aperiodic regular energy values for such a compactly supported perturbation of $H_0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture concerns realizing arbitrary compact zero-measure sets as aperiodic regular energy values for a compactly supported perturbation of an irrational ellipsoid Hamiltonian in dimension $2n\geq 6$. Counterexamples to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture at a single energy level are known (Ginzburg in high dimensions, Ginzburg–Gürel in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with $C^2$ smoothness), but no source found in the search confirms or refutes the strengthened version for arbitrary compact zero-measure sets of energy values. The status appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A C^2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in R^4
status_evidence.snippet: Ginzburg–Gürel construct a proper C^2 function on R^4 whose Hamiltonian flow has no periodic orbits on a regular level set.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples exist for a single energy value, not for arbitrary compact zero-measure sets.
